lesson_title: The Machine That Cannot Decide: Functions and Inverses
hook_text: Press 9 on this vending machine and it shrugs — 3 or minus 3? That shrug is why your exam has a restricted domain question.
clip_script: A vending machine: press a code, one snack drops. That is a function — one input, one output, every time. Now run it backwards. You hold the snack 5, and the machine y equals two x plus three tells you instantly: the code was 1. Swap x and y, solve, and the reverse machine is x minus three over two. Clean. But try the machine y equals x squared. You hold the snack 9 and ask which code produced it — and the machine shrugs. Could be 3. Could be minus 3. Both codes drop the same snack, so the reversal cannot decide, and a machine that cannot decide is not a function. The exam fix is one move: unplug half the machine. Keep only codes x greater than or equal to zero, and every snack has exactly one code — the reverse answers square root of x without hesitating. Keep the left half instead, and it answers negative square root of x. The old domain even chooses the sign for you, because old inputs become new outputs. One arm, one answer, full marks.
visual_style: A township spaza-shop vending machine with glowing code buttons, a graph parabola overlaid on its glass, the machine physically splitting down the middle at the turning point and one half powering down.
mood: Playful, mechanical, one satisfying click when the machine finally decides.
pacing: Quick presses through the working machine, a comic freeze on the shrug at 9, calm resolution as one arm is unplugged.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make any inverse answer without hesitating.
